KKA is an administrative code and data delivery mechanism used within the Danish healthcare quality infrastructure. Specifically, it refers to the specific data delivery from the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut) to regional systems, which contains data from the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] [^src1]. This delivery can be requested by hospitals and regions for local data validation purposes [^src1].

The KKA delivery allows medical staff to compare their local clinical registrations in the Electronic Patient Record (EPJ) with the data that has been reported to the National Patient Register (LPR) and subsequently forwarded to the Akut Kirurgi Databasen via KKA deliveries in the LIS systems [^src1]. This validation process is a direct trigger for practical quality improvement work across regions and hospitals, ensuring that the reported patient population accurately reflects clinical reality through precise variable definitions and hospital-level tracking [^src1]. 

For the Akut Kirurgi Databasen specifically, the designated KKA abbreviation used to identify this data delivery is "AKDB" [^src1].
